content.thinking:
I want to write the entire module in one careful pass without testing, designing a chunky Blizzard-style treant around 3.5 meters tall with oversized hands, shoulders, and head, hand-painted bark, moss, leaves, and glowing eyes. I'm planning out which utility imports I'll need for the geometry construction.

I'm now sketching the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, thick trunk-like legs, then a spine chain rising from the hips using a catmull curve, followed by a neck chain parented to the spine, working out exact joint positions and how many names/spans each chain needs to stay consistent.

For the head I'm placing it at the top of the neck pointing forward, then adding a jaw joint positioned relative to the head using local offsets. I'm starting to design the head itself as a big bark-like skull with a brow ridge and nose features.

Now I'm planning the arms, with large shoulders and chains running from the shoulder joints out to the hands in a roughly T-posed resting stance. I'm figuring out the shoulder and hand target positions and checking the resulting limb lengths work out geometrically.

Setting up the arm chains with shoulder/elbow/hand joints, then building the hand with a palm shape and finger chains branching off as separate digit roles, spreading forward and down from the wrist.

Now working out the leg structure: hip, knee, and ankle joints with calculated bend angles and lengths to reach the foot targets, tapering the limb radius from thigh to ankle, then adding a foot mass with forward toe sweeps and a back toe.

For the toes, I'll make each one a simple single-joint digit sprouting from the ankle tip, rather than a full multi-joint chain, keeping the geometry lightweight while still giving separated digits. Then I'll move on to the pelvis as a root mass and the body as a loft along the spine bones.

Now I'm working out the loft bones and torso station positions, defining pelvis, waist, chest, and shoulder cross-sections with their widths and heights along the spine chain.

Now I'm designing the shoulder pauldrons as oversized gnarled bark domes with mossy caps, positioned on the shoulder joints with scaled sphere geometry, and planning the color palette with dark browns for bark and greens for moss and leaves.

Picking the treant-style color scheme: amber glowing eyes, teal-green runes, autumn leaf tones, all kept within a limited palette. Defining bark paint functions...

Writing moss blending logic...

For the torso surface, I'm thinking about adding ridge lines by sweeping thin rod paths along the torso at various angles with alternating darker/lighter coloring, but I need to figure out which bones these ridges should follow so they bend naturally with the spine rather than staying rigid to just the hips.

Keeping the sweeps cheap with 5 sides should be fine. For the chest, I'm considering adding a glowing rune decal near the upper torso surface, positioning it close to the surface given the torso's depth, though I need to watch whether the glow effect works properly on a texture-based decal part.

I'll find the actual surface point by raycasting toward the torso instead of guessing coordinates, then use that hit point for decal placement. For the rune design itself, I'm sketching a tree-of-life glyph using teal strokes on a transparent background, sized so the stroke width scales cleanly. Then I move on to positioning the head joint and orienting it forward for attaching head parts.

Working out skull placement, I'll use a sphere scaled unevenly along world axes to shape it, centering it just above the neck joint using absolute world coordinates near the head bone rather than fiddling with local offsets.

Now I'm sketching the brow ridge as a swept curve above the eye line, layering facial bone structure outward from the skull.

For the eyes, I'm placing dark sockets behind glowing amber spheres squashed to a slit shape near the brow, giving them a core highlight for intensity. The nose becomes a gnarled, knob-like cone swept downward and tapered to feel like a broken branch.

Now I'm shaping the muzzle using a tapered box frustum for the upper jaw, then adding a row of small ivory spike teeth angled downward along its lower edge. I'm setting up the lower jaw at a hinge point near the head so it can articulate forward, with its own frustum shape beginning to take form.

Antlers branch from the head bone using swept curves with catmull splines, rising and forking into tines, with leaf cards at the tips. For the crown I'm layering leaf clusters and low-poly icosahedron foliage clumps in varying greens across the head and shoulders, watching the part count to stay under budget, and designing a simple leaf-shaped SVG texture with visible veins.

I'll make two leaf textures (green and yellow-green with orange tips), plus a moss tuft and hanging vine, and scatter cards across shoulder pauldrons, crown clumps, and arms using a surface-scatter helper with distance and filter constraints. Targeting roughly 350-450 parts total, I'm setting up the TypeScript module with careful imports and type handling to keep things clean.

Setting up imports and color palette...

Thinking about little story details too — maybe a bird nest tucked in the antlers with pale blue eggs, plus small pink blossom clusters for a cheerful touch, keeping it all moderate in quantity. Now I'm setting up the bark paint layers, blending lighter and darker grain textures with countershading and a mossy noise overlay.

Setting up the treant's skeleton...

Defining neck and head joints...

Still defining neck taper...

For the torso, I'm lofting through spine stations with widening dimensions toward the shoulders and a slight belly bulge, tapering back in at the wide pelvis base, then attaching mossy coloring and binding it to the hips/spine bone chain.

Setting hip and spine joints to their matching positions, then adding hanging root spikes around the pelvis for a skirt-like effect. For the legs, I'm computing symmetric left/right hip-to-foot targets, checking the reach distance against the two-segment leg lengths, and building each limb's three-point chain (hip, knee, ankle) with forward-bending knees.

Parenting the leg chains to the hips joint, then sweeping each leg with a tapered radius profile that bulges slightly at the knee for a more natural shape.

I'm also considering adding a small sphere burl at the knee joint for texture, and thinking about the foot/ankle terminus next.

Working out toe placement as three forward claws plus one back heel root, each a tapered capsule running from the ankle joint down into the ground, with radius shrinking from root to tip so they look like claws digging in rather than flat pads.

Now I'm adding ankle cuffs using torus rings rotated to lie flat around the leg, with moss-green shin wraps for extra detail, though I need to account for the leg's taper and forward lean when positioning them.

Still defining leg radius function...

For the arms, I'm reconsidering a more outward diagonal rest pose, repositioning the hand target farther out with elbow bending down and back, and parenting the arm chain to the chest joint of the spine.

Now I'm defining the arm's shoulder-elbow-hand chain, tapering the tube radius along its length, adding a mossy wrapped forearm bracer, and oversizing the palm as a scaled sphere.

For the fingers, I'm computing four digit chains branching from the hand position, using the forearm direction vector to orient them outward and down, with lateral spread offsets along the z-axis to splay them apart.

Still defining digit geometry...

Now I'm working out the shoulder pauldron: a scaled sphere positioned at the shoulder joint with bark plate stubs radiating outward like spikes, topped with a flattened moss cap sphere.

I'm adding mottled green moss paint and scattered leaf cards over the cap, plus small bracket-fungus shelves on the side made from flattened, tilted cylinders colored orange with cream rims. For the back, I'm planning a tree-canopy silhouette growing from the upper back and shoulders -- three big branches rising outward with foliage clumps to sell the "tree" look.

Working out the branch paths and bone attachments...

Generating foliage clusters at branch tips using small icosahedron clumps with cycling leaf colors, then scattering leaf cards across the clump surfaces for density while keeping performance manageable with around 25 clumps and 260 scattered cards.

Now I'm figuring out the leaf card orientation and hanging flow direction, filtering rock hits to avoid placing anything underneath, and sketching out the antler bone path pair from the head base outward.

Switching to absolute coordinates, I'm plotting the antler curve points rising from the head up through several waypoints, then figuring out how to place tine spikes along that sweep by computing an outward direction vector at each point.

Now I'm thinking about small foliage details on the head—tufts and sprout leaves—plus whether to add a little nest with eggs or even a tiny perched bird (body, head, beak, tail) at the head top between the antlers for a cute touch.

I'm placing the nest around y≈3.78, keeping scope manageable, then moving to the face: eyebrows, bark cheek plates, mouth line, mossy brow tufts, and glowing amber eyes positioned relative to the skull center and radius.

Working out the eye socket position on the skull surface, then angling the brows into a sharp, angry V-shape by lowering the inner points and raising the outer sweep for a fierce expression.

Now I'm placing the nose tip below the brow ridge and shaping the upper jaw as a tapered frustum extending forward from the skull, checking that its width and height narrow correctly toward the snout and sit just below the skull's base.

Still laying out the jaw geometry...

Deciding to skip the leaf-shaped ears for simplicity, and moving on to set up the glowing eye sphere.

I'm placing 14 hanging moss card frames along the jaw with slight variation for a natural beard effect, then adding similar vine frames at the cheeks, brow, and pauldron edges for extra coverage. I'm also thinking through adding bark plate detail to the chest, painting the torso with mossy textures and bark cracks, and considering overlapping extruded plates for richness.

Now I'm designing a heartwood chest plate as three stacked ridged bark pauldron shapes with shield-like outlines, planning to add a rune decal projected onto the center plate.

To find where exactly the decal should sit, I'm figuring out the plate's front face by casting a ray from above the torso down onto its surface to get an accurate hit point, then offsetting the plate placement from that.

I'll pick spine3 joint for the chest plate and torso decal, keeping belly plates attached to spine2. Checking the torso's elliptical curvature at that height, I realize the sides bulge outward relative to the plate width, so the plate thickness might need adjusting since the surface dips slightly at the edges compared to center.

I'll bump thickness to .14 to keep edges from floating free. Now defining the shield-shaped chest plate outline as a convex polygon with mild beveling, then moving on to the belly plates as overlapping horizontal bands lower on the torso.

For the belly band outlines I'm computing surface intersection heights at each y-level using a ray helper so the plates conform to the torso shape. I'm adding a glowing rune decal to the chest plate over a heartwood-grained paint base, skipping the idea of hanging tendrils on the back, and planning a draped moss "scarf" torus around the neck base.

Still working out torus placement...

I should also add the collar into the moss scatter list so tufts appear on it, and plan two separate drooping texture variants for beard-like growth and leaf blades, which I'll build as SVGs.

Still writing leaf SVGs...

I'm sizing the texture atlases, keeping leaves and cards at 128px within the 2048 limit, and planning mushroom decorations for the pauldrons using a hemisphere cap with spotted red-and-cream coloring and a cream cylinder stem.

I'm placing varying-sized mushrooms on the shoulder pauldrons, working out their positions by raycasting downward onto the curved surface so each mushroom seats naturally along the normal, with a helper function to position them at different x/z offsets.

Each mushroom is a lathe shape - a thin stem profile that flares into a rounded cap, built from an outline of points revolved around the hit normal axis to give it proper mushroom geometry.

I'll keep mushrooms upright with a fixed vertical axis and sink them slightly into the surface at the hit point, attaching them to a bone like an arm joint. For the pauldron, I'm considering a mossy cap paint and a stone pad surface, skipping bracket fungus details, and thinking about belt accessories like a small carved wooden talisman with a rune for the treant guardian.

For the belt, I'm creating a vine-like ring around the waist by cutting a loop through the torso at a spine joint, then sweeping a thin tube along that closed path with a lifted offset to simulate a vine wrapping the torso. I'll scatter small gold-wood studs evenly along that belt path using a loop that places sphere geometry at each point.

For the buckle, I'm positioning a small heart/gem shape at the front of the belt loop (angle zero, toward +Z since the torso axis runs roughly vertical), scaling a sphere slightly flattened to look like a heart-shaped gem with a glowing teal tint, double-checking the joint used for the loop plane actually lies inside the torso mesh so the cut doesn't fail.

Now I'm thinking through how to add torso ridges as sweeps — using the torso's own line method with an angle and lift, deciding whether to pass an explicit bone list (hips, spine) so the ridge follows the body's curvature correctly rather than defaulting to a single rigid bone, and sketching out the radius function that will taper each ridge along its length.

I'm also planning to alternate dark and light bark colors across the ridges for visual variation, considering whether arm segments should get similar ring bands wrapped along their chain, and deciding to skip adding ridges to the legs for now since the feet and toes are already handled.

Now I'm thinking about adding moss patches to the legs via painting, then sketching bark-flap "roots" hanging from the hips as a skirt of downward-pointing spikes, planning a ring of six to eight spikes positioned around the pelvis with base and direction vectors computed from angle around the hip circle.

I'm also adding a moss collar at the neck, hanging moss "hair" from the shoulders and antler points styled like vines, and placing small eyes with three glow accents -- chest rune, belt gem, and eyes -- plus a glowing teal torus ring around the forearm for extra detail.

Checking the triangle budget now — sweeps, spheres, and foliage icospheres all stay modest, so I'm ready to start writing the actual implementation with proper imports and types.

Writing imports and setup...

Now I'm setting up the module metadata and build function skeleton, defining the color palettes and paint functions for moss and bark using mottle, grain, and countershade utilities.

Writing paint definitions...

Defining heart grain paint, then adding a ring-drawing helper that places torus geometry along a chain at a given position.

I'm confirming ChainPoint works as a Frame and importing the Chain type from the skeleton module, then setting up torus tube radii per chain and defining arm/leg radius functions that taper with t. Now I'm writing a finger-generation helper that takes a base position, direction, segment lengths, curl amount, radius, and parent joint to build finger bones.

Working out joint naming and spans for the finger chain...

Still defining the claw spike and joint types...

Working out the hand geometry now, approximating the palm as a flattened block oriented along the forearm direction with width spread for the knuckles.

Then I'm computing finger base positions and directions from the hand center, offsetting each finger laterally across the palm and angling the thumb separately with its own base point and direction vector.

I'm also setting elbow bend hints to bulge the arms backward and downward, and defining the antler geometry as a swept path along the head bone with spike tines branching outward at several points along the curve.

Now I'm writing a helper to generate small leaf clumps as icosahedron geometries attached to bones, varying their colors randomly across a few leaf palette options, and planning the canopy layout using these clumps.

I'm placing clusters along each branch path at several points toward the tips, with radius increasing slightly near the top, giving roughly 40-45 foliage clumps total across ten branches plus some extra moss near the head and shoulders, alongside a scatter of card-based texture parts. I'm checking the overall height comes out to about 4.9 meters with feet grounded at y=0.

Now I'm verifying the leg and foot geometry so everything touches the floor correctly — checking the capsule radius tapering along the leg, the ankle joint position, and the flattened foot pad sphere's scale and position so its bottom pole sits exactly at y=0.

I'm planning the build order: joints for hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, legs, and arms first, then the torso loft, neck sweep, and limb geometry after. For toes, I'm sprouting a small tapered digit from the ankle tip joint using a two-point polyline with a shrinking radius, making sure the joint naming and radius array are set up correctly for each foot.

I'm confirming the leg joint chain order (hip, knee, ankle) resolves correctly to the tip joint, then sweeping the limbs with a smooth radius-blended skin and an 8-sided cross-section. I'm considering whether to add extra cranial details like cheek tusks or a hair crest, but deciding to skip those and move on to placing a small torus-shaped nest near the head.

Now I'm sketching out a tiny bird scene for the nest: a few speckled eggs, and a small red-bodied bird with a head, beak, and tail sitting on the head bone, keeping the part count low given the budget. I'm also weighing whether to add leaf clumps around the crown as a sort of foliage "hair" near the top of the head.

I'm scattering hundreds of leaf clumps across the surface with a minimum distance constraint, cycling through a few leaf textures, and letting the card orientation flatten against the top surface since straight-down flow doesn't work well there. Now I'm figuring out where to add moss tufts across the shoulders too.

Adding moss cards on the pauldron caps, hanging vine frames along the antlers and shoulder fronts, and checking that everything returns cleanly from the root part with proper typing and no unused locals before writing the final code.

Now I'm defining the spine curve for the antler tines using Catmull-Rom interpolation over control points, then setting up the head joint parented to the neck with its position and direction, followed by the jaw joint attachment.

For the legs, I'm looping over left and right sides, building limb curves with hip, knee, and ankle targets and a forward bend direction, then chaining the resulting points into named joints under the hips parent.

I'm verifying the leg reach fits within the limb length constraint, then adding knee burl geometry as a slightly flattened sphere, plus ring wraps and spike buttresses near the hip root. Now I'm setting up the arm limb curve with its own bend direction for the shoulder-to-hand reach.

For the arm chain I'm naming the joints shoulder/elbow/hand, parenting to the spine, and tuning a radius function so the elbow and forearm bulge slightly before tapering toward a bigger hand.

Now I'm designing the pauldron as a two-tier shoulder piece: a bark-textured lower sphere with a mossy cap on top, plus three branch-like spikes jutting outward, and I'm placing small mushrooms growing down from the cap's surface.

Still typing the mushroom scale and cap position logic...

Now I'm working out the glow ring on the forearm and need to lay out the torso before adding the chest plate, pauldrons, and collar.

For the belt, I'm sweeping a closed loop path around the torso using the spine joint as its single riding bone, since closed paths that cross a chain follow one joint reference rather than a list.

For studs, I'm placing small brass spheres along the belt path at regular intervals using a callback that positions each stud, then adding a buckle as a flattened brass sphere anchored to the front of the belt and bound to the same spine joint.

I'm rethinking plate placement so the belt and belly plates don't overlap -- shifting to a larger chest shield around y 2.42 and a lower band around y 1.62, skipping the 1.95 level entirely. Now I'm considering a mossy torus collar near the neck base and checking its height clearance.

Defining branch paths...

I'm adding larger foliage clumps at the crown top and thinking about eye glows, bark-paint texturing for the skull, and scattering small wart-like knots across the surface for extra detail.

Scattering burls on the torso with flattened sphere shapes embedded into the surface...

Now I'm adding plate shapes along the torso, computing intersection heights with a ray cast to position each plate outline correctly before extruding it, and I need to double-check I'm not importing unused helpers like lerp.

For the chest plate specifically, I'm placing a shield-shaped plate at a joint, then adding a rune decal centered on its front face using a local-space offset to find the correct surface point.

Now I'm moving on to building leaf textures for card graphics, starting with an SVG generator function that takes fill, highlight, and vein colors.

Now I'm sketching a moss tuft shape with layered leaf clusters at different depths for shading, then starting on a hanging vine shape with a tapered curve from top to bottom.

For the rune symbol, I'm drawing a circle outline with a radial spoke pattern inside, verifying the stroke width scales correctly to 10px at the 256 size target, then starting to tally up the total component counts for the final piece.

Now I'm setting up the beard cards along the chin using a grid of frame positions anchored to the jaw joint, checking that the vine root height lines up with the lower jaw box position.

I'm sketching brow moss tufts with upright small cards bound to the head joint, and planning vine frames hanging from the pauldron's lower edge at the shoulders. Finishing up with sprout geometry for the toes.

I'm computing the toe tip positions using lateral offsets for three toes plus a heel point, then wiring each sprout's polyline path from the ankle joint to its tip. Now I'm double-checking the sweep, loop/path, decal, and cards API usage against the type signatures to catch any mismatches before finalizing.

I'm confirming the surface helper handles nested Part arrays, setting up the hips joint and pelvis sphere/loft, and checking the spike function's argument order for color versus options. I'm also verifying the sweep color/paint signature, planning finger hand-target points, and setting up a filter for leaf foliage scatter based on normal direction.

Now I'm nailing down the eyebrow sweeps using catmull-spline paths with tapering radius arrays bound to the head joint, and picking final color constants for red and cream mushroom tones before writing the finished code.
